{{Short description|Dutch theoretical chemist}}
'''Ad van der Avoird''' (born 19 April 1943) is a Dutch theoretical chemist. He was professor of [[theoretical chemistry]] at the [[Radboud University Nijmegen]].

==Education and career==
Van der Avoird was born on 19 April 1943 in [[Eindhoven]].<ref name=iaqms>{{cite web|url=http://www.iaqms.org/members/vdavoird.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924032312/https://www.iaqms.org/members/vdavoird.php |title=Ad van der Avoird |publisher=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science |date= |archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> He studied at [[Eindhoven University of Technology]], obtaining his PhD under [[George Schuit]] in 1968 with a thesis titled: ''"Perturbation theory for intermolecular forces : application to some adsorption models"''.<ref>{{cite thesis|url=https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/perturbation-theory-for-intermolecular-forces-application-to-some |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331060257/https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/perturbation-theory-for-intermolecular-forces-application-to-some |title=Perturbation theory for intermolecular forces : application to some adsorption models |publisher=Eindhoven University of Technology |date= 1968|doi=10.6100/IR116131 |archive-date=31 March 2023 |last1=Avoird |first1=A Van Der }}</ref> He was professor of [[theoretical chemistry]] at the [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] and took up [[emeritus]] status in 2008 although he kept working.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.voxweb.nl/een-lintjesregen-in-de-zon/ |title=Een lintjesregen in de zon |language=Dutch |publisher=Vox |date=25 April 2014 |accessdate=19 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304103235/http://www.voxweb.nl/een-lintjesregen-in-de-zon/ |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> In 2013 Van der Avoird provided a theory on the relation between two [[benzene]] rings and their possible motion, the discovery was published with Gerard Meijer and a German research team in a paper in ''[[Angewandte Chemie]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://phys.org/news/2013-04-molecular-mystery-years.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151012032745/https://phys.org/news/2013-04-molecular-mystery-years.html |title=Molecular rings mystery solved after 20 years |publisher=[[Phys.org]] |date=16 April 2013 |archive-date=12 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.desy.de/news/@@news-view?id=5161&lang=eng |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923214128/https://www.desy.de/news/@@news-view?id=5161&lang=eng |title=Scientists decode molecule dynamics of benzene double molecule |publisher=DESY |date=6 May 2013 |archive-date=23 September 2015}}</ref> The model solved a decade old scientific issue.<ref name=fom>{{cite web|url=http://www.fom.nl/live/nieuws/archief_persberichten/persberichten2014/artikel.pag?objectnumber=262238 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924014229/http://www.fom.nl/live/nieuws/archief_persberichten/persberichten2014/artikel.pag?objectnumber=262238 |url-status=dead |title=Vier Koninklijke onderscheidingen voor de fysica |language=Dutch |publisher=Stichting voor Fundamenteel Onderzoek der Materie |date=28 April 2014 |archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
On 25 April 2014 he was made a Knight in the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]], one of only fifteen appointees that year. Amongst other accomplishments he was given the honor for his model of benzene dimer.<ref name=fom/>

Van der Avoird became member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/3813 |title=Ad van der Avoird |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=19 August 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050958/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/3813 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is also member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]].<ref name=iaqms/>
